Ara: rendering at scale

The standalone geometry/VSM slice meets the 4 ms warm static-view target on this scene. Engine fidelity and editor integration remain unfinished.

Windows 11 · RTX 4070 SUPER · driver 617.14 · Rust 1.99.1 · Vulkan SDK 1.4.363 · shared workstation · two Cargo jobs. Implementation commit 19f4c2a.

3.281 ms native 2560×1440   2.344 ms 1707×960 → 1440p
32 measured warm frames after 8 settling frames; GPU timestamps, serialized diagnostic submissions. Upscaling is linear-light bilinear. No fidelity lighting/post cost included.

1,030,942,720 instanced source triangles become 42,449 camera clusters and 2,922,000 selected triangles. Software handles 94.0% of triangle work.

The Ara shot demonstrates selection, visibility and page-cache behavior. It lacks the reference's city assets, textured material variation, indirect-light detail, reflections and atmospheric composition. UE5 visual parity has not been demonstrated.

Cold total: 18.265 ms native, 16.885 ms upscaled. The native first frame renders 10,728 shadow pages; unchanged frames reuse all of them, with zero dirty or denied pages.

Hardware-only mesh raster measures 3.107 ms; the indirect fallback measures 3.757 ms. The hybrid software path is 5.6% slower than hardware-only in these runs. Its correctness is verified; this scene does not establish a software-raster performance win.

Memory and quality

Cluster pool: 46.87 MiB, 23,996 resident pages. VSM depth pool: 1024 MiB. Total requested resources: 1419.9 MiB native / 1254.2 MiB upscaled. System VRAM after allocation: 3496 MiB; this includes other applications and is not a process peak.

  • Deterministic 1,006,780-triangle cook; decoded page round trips; every shared edge has two uses across tested DAG cuts.
  • Strict repeated/golden capture, mesh/indirect coverage and ≤1-pixel silhouette agreement with leaf geometry on the two-instance fixture. This is not a global Hausdorff bound for the billion-triangle scene.
  • Previous-HZB rejection and current-HZB disocclusion recovery, bounded feedback uploads, pinned roots, sun-cache invalidation, spot/cube pages, validation clean.
  • VSM versus full-source RT hard shadows: visibility MAE 0.051116 on 15,218 covered fixture pixels. PCF and a hard ray intentionally have different edge filters.

Integration handoff

Completed APIs: ara_geo::cook / Geometry / GeoImporter, GeometryView / Outputs / GeometryConfig, VirtualShadows / ShadowReference, and ara_vsm::directional / spot / point / Cache.

The builtin importer worker installs ara.geo with reflected settings. Fidelity must consume the exported linear surfaces and shadow visibility image through a new external-primary-surface input; its existing completed-HDR seam cannot replace primary visibility. The editor still needs extraction/publication, picking, debug routing and stats panels.

Remaining scope: full material/transform coverage; a multilevel HZB (the current conservative tile level skips large bounds); fine-grained dependency-aware streaming (the current pool publishes complete levels); incremental clipmap/caster invalidation; temporal quality and moving-camera budgets; an art-rich city benchmark; matched-hardware UE comparison. Root manifests/docs and fidelity files were left untouched.

Published comparison and reproducibility

Epic publishes roughly 2.5 ms for Nanite culling/rasterization and 2 ms for material evaluation at about 1400p on PS5. These exclude VSM and use different content/hardware, so they cannot establish relative speed against the 4070 SUPER result. Epic's published timings. No controlled 4070 SUPER Nanite comparison was available.

Run crates/ara-render-geo/run.ps1 -Mode Check, then -Mode Native or -Mode Upscaled. Captures, full per-pass JSON and stable entity maps are under crates/ara-render-geo/captures/. Tests, all-target clippy with warnings denied, formatting and shader validation pass. Integration contracts are in INTEGRATION.md. This report records the standalone slice, not completion of the entire rendering brief.
